original.target_description: Assigned original Study 1, alcohol and utilitarian judgment, locator p. 3. Full primary paper could not be acquired through the attempted open routes; target test remains unverified.

replication.target_description: Single laboratory experiment; peak blood alcohol concentration predicting binary utilitarian moral judgments in the text-based footbridge counterpart (morality and behavioural questions). No replication test locator supplied; selected BAC predictor analysis explicitly following Duke and Begue (2015).

n.location: p. 3480 (PDF p. 4), Method > Participants; Moral decision-making measures
n.quote: As such, 48 participants comprising 31 females and 17 males
n.sample_role: Participants in final experimental sample, completing moral judgment and action tasks; no additional judgment-test exclusions reported.
n.exclusions: 50 recruited; two excluded: vision problems in non-moral virtual task and failure to understand/complete that task.

es.location: p. 3486 (PDF p. 10), Results > Moral responses, final paragraph (BAC predictor analysis)

p.location: p. 3486 (PDF p. 10), Results > Moral responses, final paragraph (BAC predictor analysis)
p.quote: Peak BAC level was not a significant predictor of moral responses in the virtual moral action task (p = .575) or the moral judgment task when referencing both the morality and behavioural question (ps > .109).

reported_success.location: p. 3489 (PDF p. 13), General discussion, opening paragraph
reported_success.quote: in the present study, alcohol intake did not affect moral actions or moral judgments. These results contrast with previous findings investigating acute alcohol effects on moral decision-making.

notes: Replication reports only a shared p bound for the two moral-judgment questions in its BAC predictor analysis; no effect size or test statistic is printed for that analysis. The printed h values refer to task contrasts, not the alcohol predictor, and are not extracted. Original acquisition: DOI landing unavailable through web tool; OpenAlex supplied no best OA location; HAL record verified the title but provided only an ISTEX link, which returned HTML rather than full PDF. No statistics taken from secondary accounts or the original abstract. Replication HTML title and full Methods/Results verified; publisher PDF used to verify page locations. Supplementary material inspected; no additional statistics for the selected BAC-to-judgment analysis located.
